newsitem.title: UK: UK's Liddell warns firms on pension sales - papers.
newsitem.headline: UK's Liddell warns firms on pension sales - papers.

text.p: Treasury Economic Secretary Helen Liddell "read the riot act" to 28 of the UK's top insurance companies on Wednesday, demanding swift compensation to those who were mis-sold personal pensions, newspapers reported on Thursday.
The Independent quoted Liddell as saying continued delays in offering redress to victims were "completely unacceptable".
She said a continued lack of commitment by the companies would result in far tougher regulations being introduced as part of the government's planned reforms of the financial services industry.
The Times said Liddell had ordered the companies to report back within one month on plans to speed up compensation to more than 550,000 victims.
Sir Andrew Large and Andrew Winkler, the chairman and chief executive respectively of the regulatory body, the Securities and Investments Board, attended the meeting.
Colette Bowe, head of the Personal Investment Authority which is overseeing the 4.0 billion pounds mis-selling review, also attended.
